kind: duplicated transform-execution loop across run() and score()
title: run() and score() duplicate the non-source node execution block (input resolution + missing-input check + no-inbound-edges raise)
description: The per-non-source-node execution logic is copy-pasted between Pipeline.run() and Pipeline.score(): both compute `input_names = self._get_inputs(n.name)`, build `missing = [name for name in input_names if name not in outputs]`, raise the identical 'Node ... is missing input(s) from: ...' ValueError, gather `input_dfs = [outputs[name] for name in input_names]`, call `outputs[n.name] = n(*input_dfs)`, and otherwise raise the identical 'Node ... has no inbound edges' ValueError. The two copies are byte-for-byte equivalent apart from run() handling sources inline in the same loop while score() seeds sources in a separate prior loop. This duplication risks the two execution paths silently diverging (e.g. a future fix to the missing-input message or ordering applied to only one).
evidence: run() lines 343-357 vs score() lines 393-407 contain the same input_names/missing/input_dfs/raise structure verbatim. The only structural difference is source handling, which can be hoisted: a shared private helper, e.g. `_run_transforms(order, outputs)` iterating non-source nodes, would be called by both after each method seeds `outputs` for sources in its own way.
behavior_preservation: Extracting the shared non-source loop into one helper preserves behaviour exactly (same ordering via _get_inputs, same error messages, same _scenario_ctx token still set by each caller). Covered by existing tests: test_run, test_score, test_diamond_dependency, test_run_no_edges_raises, test_score_no_edges_raises, test_no_edges_multiple_nodes_raises.
est_reduction: ~15-18 duplicated lines collapse to a single ~10-line helper.
